subject: Re: Model fit / evals follow-up — tool-calling & structured output validation
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwoodinference.com>
To: Emma Rodriguez <emma@averyanalytics.com>
Cc: Sean Gallagher <sean_gallagher@redwoodinference.com>
Date: 2027-03-14T15:02:00-07:00
Subject: Thanks for the demo — next steps on evals and tool-calling

Hi Emma,

Thanks for taking the time today — great discussion. Quick recap and proposed next steps from our side: 

- Objective: validate model fit for Avery’s customer support summarization and structured ticket extraction pipelines (JSON output).
- Ask from Avery: benchmark accuracy on your historical dataset, function/tool-calling reliability (retries, idempotency), and JSON schema compliance for structured output.

Proposed next steps: 
1) We’ll run a 2-day eval using the sample dataset you shared in the call (or the export link you send).
2) We’ll test three model+config combos we recommend for this workload: Redwood-optimized Llama2-13b (quant-pt-8), RedModel-3-small (int8), and an LLM with our function-calling strict mode.
3) Deliverables: benchmark report (accuracy, F1 on entity extraction), prompt set used, examples of schema-compliant outputs + failure modes, and suggested retry/backoff policy for tool calls.

Can you confirm the dataset we should use (full export vs sampled subset) and whether we can run with anonymized PII? Also, please share any firm SLOs for latency and acceptable failure rates for schema noncompliance.

I attached the post-call notes and a suggested mutual action plan. We’ll kick off once you confirm.

Best,
Marissa
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
marissa@redwoodinference.com
(415) 555-0123

Subject: Re: Thanks for the demo — next steps on evals and tool-calling

Hi Marissa — thanks for the clear recap. Confirming a few items: 

- Dataset: please run the evals on our 6-week export (anonymized) — link below. If you need a smaller sample for quick iteration, use the first 5k rows but run final benchmarks on the full 120k rows.
- PII: we can provide an anonymized export; we’ll send a hashed version (no direct identifiers).
- SLOs: for production we target median token latency < 250ms and schema compliance >= 99% for final outputs; for the eval we care most about quality/ease of remediation.

Links/attachments:
- Drive: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1AveryEvalBenchmarks
- Attached: a short benchmark spec (avery_benchmarks_v1.pdf)

One question on the model list — can you also include a smaller low-cost model for baseline comparisons (we’re sensitive to inference cost)?

Thanks — I’ll loop in Security once we have the anonymized export.

—Emma

Head of ML Platforms | Avery Analytics
emma@averyanalytics.com

From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwoodinference.com>
To: Emma Rodriguez <emma@averyanalytics.com>
Cc: Sean Gallagher <sean_gallagher@redwoodinference.com>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwoodinference.com>
Date: 2027-03-16T09:10:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Thanks for the demo — next steps on evals and tool-calling

Thanks Emma — perfect. We’ll include a cost-focused baseline (Redwood Tiny-1) alongside the three configs I mentioned. 

High-level eval plan (short):
- Models to test: Redwood-optimized Llama2-13b (quant-pt-8), RedModel-3-small (int8), Redwood Tiny-1 (baseline).
- Tests: structured extraction accuracy (F1), JSON schema validation rate, hallucination rate on key fields, token latency distribution, and cost per 1k responses.
- Tool/function-calling checks: simulate downstream calls (createTicket(payload)), ensure idempotency, test retries/backoff and last-resort fallback to text-only summary if schema fails.
- Prompt sets: we’ll run 3 prompt variants for each model; I attached the prompt_sets_v2.json with template examples and required schema.

Deliverables & timeline:
- Day 0 (today): confirm dataset link and we get anonymized export from you.
- Day 1-2: run small-sample iterations (~5k rows) and produce early results.
- Day 3-5: full-run benchmarks and a report with recommended model + config, prompt set, and a remediation plan for schema failures.

Notes on JSON schema compliance: to reduce brittle failures we’ll: 
- Use strict schema validator at post-generation (we’ll provide the schema file).
- Add a lightweight wrapper that attempts 2 auto-corrections (simple fixes like closing brackets, enforcing types) before marking as noncompliant.
- If noncompliant after corrections, we’ll retry function call with a deterministic prompt-based repair step, up to 2 retries, then fallback.

I’ve attached the prompt sets and the sample schema we’ll validate against. Will start runs once we have the anonymized export link.

Best,
Marissa

Attachments: prompt_sets_v2.json, structured_output_schema.json

From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwoodinference.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwoodinference.com>, Emma Rodriguez <emma@averyanalytics.com>
Cc: Sean Gallagher <sean_gallagher@redwoodinference@redwoodinference.com>
Date: 2027-03-17T11:45:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Thanks for the demo — next steps on evals and tool-calling

Looping in some implementation notes from the runtime team: 

- Retries: Our tests show 2 controlled retries with exponential backoff (200ms -> 600ms) recovers ~85% of schema failures due to minor formatting errors. The retry prompt should be deterministic to avoid different hallucinated values.
- Idempotency: For createTicket calls include a client-generated idempotency_key; if the model generates slightly different payload shapes we canonicalize before sending downstream.
- Metrics to capture during the run: schema_validation_rate, post-repair_success_rate, avg_retries_per_failed_call, percent_fallbacks, median_token_latency. Please ensure these are logged at token-level granularity for cost attribution.

Happy to help with the test harness — I can drop a small sample harness that runs locally against the anonymized export.

—Rishi
Rishi Malhotra
Senior Applied ML Engineer | Redwood Inference
